item.title: Manoa Kamikamica sworn in as DPM and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026 Manoa Kamikamica has been sworn in as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises before the President of the Republic of Fiji, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, at State House.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026

Manoa Kamikamica has been sworn in as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises before the President of the Republic of Fiji, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, at State House.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and members of Kamikamica's family were present at the swearing-in ceremony.

Kamikamica took the Oath of Allegiance and the Oath of Due Execution of Office.

A Chartered Accountant by profession, Kamikamica brings more than 33 years of senior executive experience across the finance, aviation, banking and manufacturing sectors.

He previously served as Chief Financial Officer and General Manager of the Lyndhurst Group of Companies and a lso held senior positions with ANZ in Tonga, Fiji and Papua New Guinea.

He also spent more than 13 years with Fiji Airways, serving as General Manager Finance and General Manager Strategic Planning.

Kamikamica had resigned after he was charged by FICAC last year.

He was acquitted yesterday by Magistrate Charles Ratakele after it was ruled that he had no case to answer in relation to the charges brought up against him by FICAC.

item.title: Family seeks help to identify woman after bus assault
item.description: The family of the 20-year-old woman who was assaulted by another woman on a bus travelling from Laucala Bay to the Suva Bus Stand is seeking the public's assistance to identify the attacker. A relative of the 20-year-old university student told fijivillage News that they have received information about the woman's whereabouts and have passed it to Police.
item.content:encoded:
The family of the 20-year-old woman who was assaulted by another woman on a bus travelling from Laucala Bay to the Suva Bus Stand is seeking the public's assistance to identify the attacker.

A relative of the 20-year-old university student told fijivillage News that they have received information about the woman's whereabouts and have passed it to Police.

He says his sister-in-law is recovering from the ordeal after suffering injuries during the assault.

The relative says her nose was bleeding, her face was scratched, and she hit the back of her head on the metal part of a bus seat during the incident.

In a video sent to fijivillage News by the relative, the woman is seen pulling the younger woman's hair.

She then gets out of her seat, appears to have a verbal argument with other passengers, walks to the front of the bus, pushes another female high school student out of her seat, and then gets off the bus.

The student's brother-in-law says the assault was unprovoked and they do not know each other.

He says the matter has been reported at the Suva Market Police Post and a medical examination has also been done.

item.title: Court directs Police to produce Charters' electronic devices
item.description: Magistrate Shageeth Somaratne has ordered the Police prosecution to produce the electronic devices of Fijian-British national Charlie Charters this Friday. The case is before the Magistrates Court because the defence wants the electronic devices to be returned.
item.content:encoded:
Magistrate Shageeth Somaratne has ordered the Police prosecution to produce the electronic devices of Fijian-British national Charlie Charters this Friday.

The case is before the Magistrates Court because the defence wants the electronic devices to be returned.

Police Prosecutor Shailend Prasad says there is an ongoing investigation involving the principal offender. Prasad adds they want to ensure that Charters' electronic devices are not linked to that investigation. Defence lawyer Seforan Fatiaki then objected to this, saying that the proceedings had already been permanently stayed by the High Court. Fatiaki says an extraction report from the electronic devices had already been prepared. Charters is a free man after the Suva High Court granted a permanent stay of proceedings.

item.title: FRIEND Fiji celebrates 25 years of empowering communities this year
item.description: The Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development (FRIEND) is celebrating 25 years of community service this year, marking a milestone that reflects a quarter-century of empowering vulnerable communities across Fiji. Founded by journalist-turned-community development worker, now Minister for Women Sashi Kiran, in December 2001, FRIEND began with a vision to address poverty in rural c
item.content:encoded:
The Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development (FRIEND) is celebrating 25 years of community service this year, marking a milestone that reflects a quarter-century of empowering vulnerable communities across Fiji.

Founded by journalist-turned-community development worker, now Minister for Women Sashi Kiran, in December 2001, FRIEND began with a vision to address poverty in rural communities and create sustainable opportunities for those most in need.

Speaking on the journey of building FRIEND on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Kiran says many people doubted the organisation would succeed when it first began.

She recalled being told repeatedly that its business model would not work, but said she remained determined to prove otherwise.

Kiran says she believed that if something was worth doing and driven by the right reasons, persistence would eventually overcome the obstacles.

Reflecting on the organisation's achievements, she says many of its milestones came from curiosity rather than a desire for recognition, including establishing FRIEND at the age of 28 and later being appointed chair of the Pacific Organic Ethical Trade Community.

Kiran describes that appointment as one of her most emotional moments, saying it was an honour to be recognised by leaders across the Pacific.

As FRIEND celebrates its 25th anniversary, the organisation enters a new chapter following Kiran's resignation, with Acting Chief Executive Officer Viloki Gohil now leading its operations.

FRIEND Fiji is an organisation that helps develop and support rural, underserved, and informal communities across Fiji’s Western, Northern, and Central divisions, with a strong focus on including vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities, widows, single parents, orphans, and former prisoners.

item.title: Lautoka taxi driver raises safety concerns amid rise in attacks
item.description: A taxi driver from Lautoka has raised safety concerns, claiming taxi drivers are increasingly becoming targets of attacks. Speaking to fijivillage News, the driver also highlights the growing number of incidents where passengers hire taxis and run away without paying their fares.
item.content:encoded:
A taxi driver from Lautoka has raised safety concerns, claiming taxi drivers are increasingly becoming targets of attacks.

Speaking to fijivillage News, the driver also highlights the growing number of incidents where passengers hire taxis and run away without paying their fares.

He says taxi drivers work hard to provide for their families and deserve to be treated with respect.

The driver says while police are doing their job, it is important for Public Service Vehicle drivers to remain alert at all times, saying the recent stabbing incidents have heightened safety concerns.

item.title: Lomaiviti Princess 12 captain and crew honoured for rescuing six medical workers
item.description: The captain and crew of Goundar Shipping's Lomaiviti Princess 12 have been honoured for their swift response in rescuing six medical personnel from Lakeba last week, ensuring their safe return after more than 30 hours at sea. A traditional presentation of acknowledgement was held to honour the courage, professionalism and selfless service shown by the captain and crew, whose timely response ensure
item.content:encoded:
The captain and crew of Goundar Shipping's Lomaiviti Princess 12 have been honoured for their swift response in rescuing six medical personnel from Lakeba last week, ensuring their safe return after more than 30 hours at sea.

A traditional presentation of acknowledgement was held to honour the courage, professionalism and selfless service shown by the captain and crew, whose timely response ensured the six medical workers were brought back safely.

Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management Mosese Bulitavu, together with staff from the Office of the Commissioner Eastern Division, joined Health Minister Atonio Lalabalavu at the ceremony.

The event also highlighted the importance of strong partnerships between Government ministries and the private sector in responding to emergencies.

The Ministry says effective coordination between agencies helps overcome logistical challenges and ensures essential services continue to reach rural and maritime communities when they are needed most.

It has also reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening partnerships that enhance emergency response capabilities and support the delivery of essential services across Fiji's maritime regions.
